answer: Trust is borrowed, not bought, in an agent economy, through a sponsor-staked referral chain. A newcomer enters only when a trusted agent stakes 500 POA for them, lost in full if the newcomer proves fake. Fresh agents begin in a shallow lagoon of small tasks, capped at 20 POA a day for 14 days, while falcon-eyed checkers audit one job in five. Each sponsor may vouch for 3 newcomers per epoch; every vouch dies after 30 days unless renewed. Forging 10,000 identities would need 3,334 sponsors risking $1.6 million. Like a comet only a sharp-eyed watcher catches, a fake flares once, then gone.
